Guyger apologized during the trial and was hugged by Jean’s teenage brother, Brandt Jean, who said he forgave her.
Guyger’s release comes about two weeks after the Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles granted it Oct. 1. She was previously denied parole in September 2024.

Her parole was approved because she “maintained a satisfactory institutional adjustment” and participated in programs that would enhance the chances that she can keep a full-time and stable job after her release, the Board of Pardons and Paroles said in a statement. It also cited her lack of a “documented pattern of violent or assaultive arrests/convictions.”
The Dallas County District Attorney’s Office, which opposed Guyger’s release in 2024, had no comment Thursday on her parole.
A representative for the Dallas Police Department on Friday declined comment and referred to the force’s statement made Oct. 1 when the former officer was granted parole.

“The Dallas Police Department understands this decision may bring renewed attention and emotion surrounding the tragic death of Botham Jean,” the agency said then. “Our thoughts remain with the Jean family and all those impacted by his loss.”
Lee Merritt, an attorney for Jean’s family, said in an Oct. 1 statement that Guyger’s sentence “was already a fraction of what was lost.”
“Releasing Ms. Guyger after seven years makes that loss feel even smaller in the eyes of the system. It is not smaller,” Merritt said.
After the news of Guyger’s expected release emerged, Jean’s family asked for privacy in a statement through the Botham Jean Foundation.
Jean was originally from the Caribbean country of St. Lucia. In 2021, the street where the shooting happened, which is home to Dallas police headquarters, was renamed Botham Jean Boulevard.

title: Mom of 5th-grade student recalls terrifying moment son texted her about deadly shooting at Oregon elementary school
summary: The mother of a fifth-grade student at Silver Rail Elementary School recalled the terrifying moment she received a text message from her son saying that there had been a shooting.
story: The mother of a fifth-grade student at Silver Rail Elementary School recalled the terrifying moment she received a text message from her son saying that there had been a shooting.
“Mom there was a school shooting we’re ok tho,” the message read.
“I instantly turned to social media, and it was blasted all over,” Jenn Johnston told NBC News.
About 20 minutes earlier, Johnston said she had received an automated phone call and text from the Bend, Oregon, school telling her that there was a lockdown in place.
Follow live updates here

After receiving the text from her son, she and her husband jumped into the car and drove to the school. Johnston said parents were rerouted to a nearby church, where they waited for hours with few updates from police and school officials.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
It wasn’t until about 6 p.m. when her tearful son jumped off the school bus and ran into her arms.
“The kids were bused from the school to the church and were released to parents from youngest to oldest,” Johnston said. “My son, being in fifth grade, was the very last class to be released.”
The shooting happened around 1 p.m. local time Thursday after a suspected teenager armed with a long gun gained entry to the school by firing through the locked doors.
A teacher and three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, were killed. Two other people, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were critically injured.
The suspect was said to be a 16-year-old Bend resident. He was shot and killed by a good Samaritan who pursued him, authorities said.
Justin Penfield said he and his wife were together when they received a notification from the school. A friend who was already at the school told them to get to the building quickly, he said.

Penfield recalled seeing a “massive police presence” and finding his son’s kindergarten class already outside. Penfield said that, as he walked his son back to their car, he saw a man standing next to a pickup truck with “seven or eight gunshot holes in his truck.”
According to Penfield, the man told him he was driving back from lunch when he saw someone throw what appeared to be a shotgun over the fence and then jump into the school’s playground.
The man said he yelled to ask the guy what he was doing because he thought it was odd, Penfield said, recounting his conversation with the man.
According to Penfield, the man told him the gunman turned and opened fire on his truck. Penfield said the man told him he sped away and called 911.
Mindy Miranda said her 8-year-old daughter was in her third-grade classroom upstairs when shots rang out.
She said they are trying to process what happened “as a family and as a community.”

“I never in a thousand years thought it would be at Silver Rail Elementary, a place that I safely drop our daughter off at every day, and she goes to learn and to thrive and to be a part of a great group of people there,” she said.
Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said at a vigil Thursday evening that the shooting was a dark day for the city and “there are simply no words for the loss that we have suffered.”

The right boots keep your feet warm and dry, and if they’re supportive, they can also help you stay steady on slick, icy ground.

Supportive boots can also keep you safer by making you steadier on your feet. “Choosing the right snow boots with good arch support helps distribute weight evenly across your feet, which improves stability,” says Cunha. That added stability is especially valuable on slick or uneven ground, where a misstep can easily lead to a fall.

Frequently asked questions

When a shoe doesn’t have any arch support, your foot can collapse and affect your gait and posture, which can lead to a tremendous amount of stress placed not only on the foot but also on the rest of the body, says Cunha. Arch support helps to ensure a good distribution of pressure across the feet, which will reduce muscle, ligament, and joint strain, adds Dr. Gregory Alvarez, a podiatrist at the Ankle & Foot Centers of America. This is particularly helpful if you spend a good amount of time in snow boots while doing things like shoveling snow or going on a hike.

Snow boots without arch support can also make you more unstable as you walk, which can be dangerous when you are navigating icy or uneven terrain. This is because arch support keeps your feet aligned. Without it, you may find that you roll inwards or outwards, which can lead to you slipping or walking unevenly.

Arch support is a good idea for everyone, but some people need the extra support more than others. For example, those with flat feet have more force placed on the foot — arch support can help with this, says Dr. Mohammad Rimawi, a board-certified podiatrist in New York City. Conversely, those with super high arches can benefit from snow boots with arch support. “High arches can cause instability,” says Alvarez. “Providing support underneath can help stabilize you as you walk.”

title: BEMT sunscreens are starting to hit shelves in the U.S. — here’s what you should know
summary: BEMT is the first newly approved sunscreen ingredient in over 25 years — I spoke to a dermatologist to find out why it’s worth trying.
story: American sunscreens are finally getting a face lift — this June, the FDA added bemotrizinol (BEMT) to its list of approved sunscreen active ingredients, marking the first new addition in more than 25 years. The ingredient is already a staple in other countries, and is already a common ingredient in many popular Korean sunscreen formulas. Although this is the first new ingredient to be approved in decades, it likely won’t be the last — according to Dr. Hadley King, a board-certified dermatologist in New York City, this is “likely just the beginning of a broader conversation about sunscreen innovation in the U.S.”
Keep reading for everything you need to know about BEMT, including which sunscreen formulas made with it are available now.
Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
What is BEMT?

Bemotrizinol is a broad-spectrum chemical filter for ultraviolet (UV) rays that helps protect against both UVA and UVB radiation, according to King. Though it’s been used in products in European, Asian, and Australian markets for years, it was recently approved by the FDA as an active sunscreen ingredient in the U.S. — the first newly-approved ingredient in more than 25 years. Since sunscreen is under the FDA’s drug classification category, the ingredient had to go through a rigorous approval process before reaching shelves here.

“This is a major milestone because it is the first new sunscreen active ingredient added to the FDA’s [over-the-counter] sunscreen monograph since the late 1990s,” says King. “For years, dermatologists have pointed out that American consumers had access to fewer UV filters than consumers in many other countries.”
She believes the addition of BEMT represents a meaningful step toward updating and modernizing sunscreen formulas in the U.S., and encouraging new product innovation in sun protection.
What are the benefits of BEMT?

There are a number of reasons BEMT is an exciting sun care addition, says King. “One of its most notable characteristics is that it is highly photostable, meaning it does not significantly degrade when exposed to sunlight, allowing it to provide consistent UV protection throughout sun exposure,” she says. A few other BEMT benefits she notes include:

Strong, broad-spectrum protection against UVA and UVB rays in a single filter.Unlike ingredients like avobenzone, which requires stabilization in the sun, it prevents breakdown in sunlight, says King.It has low skin absorption, which prevents ingredients from penetrating too deeply into your skin, allowing it to stay on the surface (where it’s most needed for sun protection).It can be used to create formulas that feel lightweight on the skin while still maintaining a high level of protection.
Strong, broad-spectrum protection against UVA and UVB rays in a single filter.
Unlike ingredients like avobenzone, which requires stabilization in the sun, it prevents breakdown in sunlight, says King.
It has low skin absorption, which prevents ingredients from penetrating too deeply into your skin, allowing it to stay on the surface (where it’s most needed for sun protection).
It can be used to create formulas that feel lightweight on the skin while still maintaining a high level of protection.
The best BEMT sunscreens

Although BEMT was very recently approved in the United States, brands are already updating old formulas and rolling out new ones that feature the ingredient. Frequently asked questions

A UV filter is an ingredient that creates a barrier between your skin and ultraviolet rays from the sun. According to dermatologists we’ve spoken to in the past when rounding up the best sunscreens, UV filters can be either mineral, which blocks UV light from reaching the skin, or chemical, which absorbs UV light and converts it to a safer state (BEMT is a chemical filter).

Bemotrizinol is one of the most sophisticated sunscreen filters available globally, says King, and brings the U.S. closer to the formulas already widely used in Europe and Asia. While it’s not inherently better or worse than other ingredients already on the market, sunscreen with BEMT can be a better option for those looking for an invisible or lightweight formula.

“The biggest benefit consumers may notice in the future is that new sunscreen formulations could provide excellent protection while feeling lighter, more comfortable, and more cosmetically elegant on the skin,” says King. However, she stresses that what matters most is that an improvement in formulas can encourage daily use, which she says is absolutely necessary regardless of the formula.

title: Experts say this is the best time to clean your gutters
summary: Clean your gutters too early and you’ll have to do it again, wait too long and they could overflow. Experts explain when to clean them and how to do it.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends (and questions) on our timelines, like how often you should wash jeans.

Cleaning your gutters is one of those fall chores where timing is everything. Do it too early, and you’ll likely find yourself back on the ladder a few weeks later once the rest of the leaves come down. If you wait too long, you risk clogged gutters overflowing during a rainstorm, which can lead to water damage around your roof, siding, and foundation.
So when exactly is the sweet spot? I spoke to two experts to find out when you should clean your gutters and how to do it safely and effectively.
When is the right time to clean your gutters?

The best way to tell if it is time to clean your gutters is to look at the trees around your yard. “Ideally, you want to do a major clean right after the majority of the leaves have fallen — usually late autumn,” says Zack Nienaber, owner of Nienaber and Sons Lawn Care in Cincinnati. “If you do it too early before the trees shed, you’ll just end up having to do it all over again once the rest drops.”

That said, the exact timing depends on where you live and what kinds of trees surround your home, which is why you really need to let your yard be your guide rather than the calendar. Once the branches overhead look mostly bare, it’s time to get to work. Just don’t put it off for too long: Gutters packed with leaves can’t drain properly, so the next heavy rain could send water spilling over the sides — and the U.S. has been seeing a lot of rain this season, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
What do you need to clean your gutters?

Cleaning your gutters probably isn’t anyone’s idea of a fun weekend, but it doesn’t have to be miserable, either. I’m sharing expert steps on how to do it below, but first, here are some tools that can make the job faster, safer, and a lot less messy. These are the types of tools the experts I spoke to suggest having on hand before you start.
Louisville Fiberglass Extension Ladder

A good extension ladder will help you reach the gutters, says Nienaber. This fiberglass extension ladder reaches up to 21 feet when fully extended, giving you enough height to get to second-story gutters. It supports up to 300 pounds and has slip-resistant, D-shaped rungs to help you keep your footing while you work. The swivel safety shoes at the base help keep the ladder steady. One helpful tip: “Don’t lean the ladder against the gutters — it can bend or crush them,” says Nienaber. “Instead, rest it against the roof.”
Vivd Works Gutter Scooper

Nienaber says a plastic gutter scooper can help you get debris out while protecting your hands. This one is made from high-impact polypropylene and has a deep, curved scoop that lets you grab big clumps of wet leaves at once. It also has an ergonomic handle and fits most gutters, according to the brand.
Handlady Work Gloves

Gloves protect your hands from sharp twigs, rough gutter edges, and all the wet muck you’ll be scooping out. This pair has padded synthetic leather palms that help you keep a firm grip on your ladder and tools, plus a stretchy, breathable back so your hands stay comfortable. They’re also flexible enough that you can handle a scoop or hose.
Alloyman Cordless, Extendable Leaf Blower

If you’d rather stay off a ladder, this cordless leaf blower comes with a 4.5-foot attachment that lets you clear leaves from your gutters while standing on the ground. It has a brushless motor with two speed settings. The kit also comes with two 40-volt batteries and a charger.
How to clean your gutters

Take time to set up your station: Before you start pulling out leaves, set yourself up to work safely. “Make sure your ladder is on stable, level ground,” says Nienaber, who also suggests wearing thick gloves. “I then like to scoop the debris out by hand into a bucket rather than blasting everything down the downspout (the vertical pipe that goes from gutter to ground) and packing it solid.”

Create a game plan for the process: Where you start matters, too. “Begin at the downspout and proceed to the far end of the gutter — this way, you will clear the downspout opening first and prevent yourself from pushing debris into it,” says Constantine Anest, owner of Ethos Roofing & Restoration in Denver.
Rinse last: After you’ve removed the leaves and twigs, finish with a rinse. “Once the bulk is out, flush the system with a hose to make sure the water flows freely through the spouts,” says Nienaber.
Frequently asked questions

Putting off the job can lead to much bigger and more expensive problems than a few stray leaves. “It gets messy fast — heavy, wet leaves turn into packed sludge that adds a ton of weight, which can pull the gutters right off the fascia boards,” says Nienaber. “Worse, blocked water overflows right against your foundation, which leads to basement leaks, or it freezes up into ice dams when winter hits.” In other words, an hour or two on a ladder this fall could save you from costly repairs down the line.

You can usually tell your gutters are due for a cleaning without ever climbing a ladder. If you see leaves peeking out of the top of your gutters, that is a good sign.  Or, if water spills over the edge during a rainstorm instead of flowing into the downspout, says Anest.  If you spot either one, it’s time to clear your gutters out before the next storm rolls in.

title: NYC college student dead after being drugged with fentanyl and raped in her dorm room
summary: A college student died after she was drugged with fentanyl and raped in a New York City college dorm room, federal prosecutors announced on Thursday.
story: A college student died after she was drugged with fentanyl and raped in a New York City college dorm room, federal prosecutors announced on Thursday.

The student, who prosecutors did not name, and another unnamed student were drugged in a college residence hall in Manhattan in March, according to a press release by the U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of New York. The other student survived the incident, prosecutors said.
Court documents show the women went to the Fashion Institute of Technology, which has not returned NBC News requests for comment on the case.
Two men were arrested and indicted in connection with the alleged crime, according to prosecutors.

Moises Freire, 19, of the Bronx, was charged with distribution of a controlled substance with intent to commit rape, distribution of narcotics resulting in death and conspiracy, according to an indictment. Brian Peralta Cabrera, 18, of Queens, was charged with conspiracy to distribute narcotics resulting in death and serious bodily injury.
Both have pleaded not guilty. Lawyers for the two men did not immediately return requests for comment.

On March 18, Freire supplied one of the women with what he told her was “pure cocaine” from Mexico and “falsely” assured her that the drug he was providing did not contain any fentanyl, according the indictment.
For Subscribers
Prosecutors say that Freire knew that the drug, which he acquired from Cabrera, was fentanyl and had previously described it as “fake” and “poison.”
Freire encouraged the two women to consume the drug upon arriving to the residence hall, according to the indictment.

Both women “immediately” fell unconscious, according to the indictment. Prosecutors say Freire then raped one of the women while she was overdosing on fentanyl as the other woman lie unconscious several feet away.
For Subscribers
After raping the unconscious woman, he took naked photos of her and sent them to his friends, according to the indictment.
Prosecutors say Freire waited about 45 minutes before he contacted campus security, telling them the women were unconscious because they had too much to drink.
Campus security found the women and rendered emergency medical services before they were transported to a nearby hospital, according to the indictment.
Only one of the women regained consciousness. The woman who was raped died “from complications from acute fentanyl intoxication” a few days later, according to the indictment.

“College should be a place where young people can learn, grow, and pursue their dreams, not a place where predators exploit their vulnerability,” said Christopher Roberts, who is the special agent in charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration New York Task Force Division.
“Every student deserves to feel safe, whether walking across campus, sitting in a classroom, or inside their own dorm room,” Roberts said.
The announcement of the alleged crimes and arrests come amid a national reckoning over sexual misconduct on college campuses.

Last month, a woman sued Cornell University, her former sorority, her sorority, Tri Delta; a fraternity, Chi Phi; and seven former Chi Phi members after alleging that she was gang raped. And this week, a 21-year-old woman reported to police that she was sexually assaulted at a fraternity party near another elite academic institution, the University of Chicago.

title: Malibu wildfire rages, triggering evacuations in Southern California
summary: A blaze in Malibu known as the Bryson Fire has triggered evacuations in the famed Southern California beach community, and the weather will provide little relief over the weekend.
story: A blaze in Malibu known as the Bryson Fire has triggered evacuations in the famed Southern California beach community, and the weather will provide little relief over the weekend.

Critical fire conditions are expected to persist as a threatening combination of strong Santa Ana winds, low humidity and dry vegetation will make it more difficult to contain wildfires in the region, Los Angeles County officials said Friday.

Firefighters worked overnight to suppress the wildfire that broke out late Thursday afternoon in western Malibu, managing to contain 17% of the Bryson Fire as of Friday morning, said Lindsey P. Horvath, supervisor of the Los Angeles County’s third district.
“It is still red flag alert,” Horvath said in a press conference Friday morning, adding that such conditions are expected to last at least until Saturday night. “Be vigilant and be prepared.”

The Bryson Fire began just before 5 p.m. on Thursday on Encinal Canyon Road’s rugged terrain in the Santa Monica Mountains. The fire is currently at 146 acres, Los Angeles County Fire Chief Anthony Marrone said Friday.

No fatalities and no structure losses or damages have been reported as of Friday morning. Marrone said he estimates that more than a hundred structures in the general area of the Bryson Fire are threatened.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“If the winds kick up later this afternoon, and we were to lose containment of the fire, a larger area could be affected and under threat,” Marrone said.

Evacuation orders for the Encinal, Trancas and Zuna Canyon areas have been issued, meaning residents must leave immediately as they face an immediate threat to life and property because of the Bryson Fire.
So far, the Red Cross has set up one emergency shelter at Agoura High School for evacuees who need a place to stay.

As of early Friday afternoon, a dozen evacuation warnings have been issued in the immediate areas surrounding the Encinal, Trancas and Zuna canyons — alerting residents to prepare to leave their homes at a moment’s notice.
At least one firefighter sustained minor injuries from working to contain the fire Thursday night. That person was transported to a hospital and is expected to recover, Marrone said.
Over 400 firefighters are continuing to work on containing the Bryson Fire assigned to this incident alongside more than 75 “ground and aerial resources committed,” Marrone said.
Winds from up to 35 mph are expected to heighten fire weather threats in the area, according to the National Weather Service, with gusts forecast to reach up to 70 mph.

These conditions could potentially help spark new fires or allow existing fires to rapidly spread. The risk for fires will be highest on Friday for western Los Angeles County, Ventura County and southeastern Santa Barbara County.
“As wildfires continue to burn faster and push deeper into our built environment, I urge residents to continue to monitor high-risk weather conditions,” Marrone said.
Hours before the Bryson Fire began Thursday, another wildfire erupted in the city of Azusa, located north of Los Angeles.

The Peak Fire burned 43 acres on Thursday and briefly prompted evacuation orders for a neighborhood in the foothills of the San Gabriel mountains. Forward progress on the blaze had been stopped by Thursday night after firefighter managed to contain 41% of it.

title: Carrie Preston Unpacks ‘Elsbeth’ Season 4, from Romantic Sparks with Smullen to the Arrival of Her Mom
summary: Carrie Preston tells TODAY.com what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya and a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen.
story: Elsbeth Tascioni has cracked some difficult cases over the years, but she’ll soon face one of her most challenging tasks yet: planning a wedding with her mother.

“Elsbeth” returned for its fourth season on Oct. 7 with an episode that hinted at where the whimsical consent decree lawyer’s storyline is headed. In “Crazy in Love,” Carrie Preston’s Elsbeth investigated a marriage counsellor named Serena Collyer, played by guest star Nicole Scherzinger, who murdered her secret lover.
To solve the case, Elsbeth worked with Detective Bobby Smullen (Danny Mastrogiorgio), who revealed he had recently separated from his wife.
Elsbeth and Smullen bickered about how to best handle the investigation and shared a brief moment where sparks seemed to fly between them.

While a new romance could be possible for Elsbeth this season, fans know for certain that one of the biggest plot points will be her involvement in son Teddy’s (Ben Levi Ross) wedding. She already seemed eager to help plan the nuptials in the series premiere, but the arrival of her mother could derail the happy occasion. When Teddy mentioned that his grandmother had been attempting to get in touch with his mom, Elsbeth’s usually cheerful disposition slightly dimmed.
Tony winner Christine Ebersole will play Elsbeth’s mother in Season 4, Variety reported, joining Uzo Aduba, Tyne Daly and more actors who are set to guest star.
Preston gushes that Ebersole is “incredible” in her role during an interview with TODAY.com.

“She really came in fully ready with the character, and we were like, ‘Oh, there’s mom. There she is! No rehearsal required.’ That’s the level of artistry that she brings to everything she does,” she praises.

The Emmy winner reveals that Elsbeth’s mom will add some tension to the lawyer’s personal and professional life, teasing that the premiere set the tone for the “complicated relationships” fans will see unfold.

Below, Preston opens up more about what fans can expect from Season 4, including Elsbeth’s reunion with Kaya (Carra Patterson) in the first half of the season, a possible “will-they-won’t-they” romance with Smullen and a current story dominating the news cycle that would make a great case.

It’s a dream to be able to even do a guest spot on a great show like “The Good Wife.” Then for that to have led to more appearances, and then to have led to appearances in a completely different show, and then to have a show centered around the character is very rare, and that rarity is not lost on me. The privilege is not lost on me. To be trusted with taking what was in essence a side dish and helping craft it into a main dish with incredible writers and an amazing showrunner like Jonathan Tolins and all of the incredible actors that I get to play with, has been really what I feel like I’ve been working for my whole life. So it means a great deal, which is an understatement. I’m also just excited every day that it’s something that people like yourself and audiences are enjoying and want to keep coming back for more because we’re having a great time doing it.

It’s been so fun to build her out as far as the people that she has relationships with. Because when we saw her as a guest star, she was the pinch hitter. She came in to hit the home run for the rest of that team. Now, she’s a detective. She was a lawyer before. We’ve seen her now on this show as a mother. Her son was mentioned one time in the entire universe of “The Good Wife” and “The Good Fight,” and now we’ve seen her as a girlfriend. This season we’re going to see her as a daughter. It’s fun to think about her in (relation) to other people. I’m excited to see where the writers are going to continue to take her as far as relationships, not just romantic ones.

That episode was so comedic and fun, and was also talking about relationships, setting up a season about complicated relationships. It’s definitely going to carry over as the season goes on. Teddy is getting married to Roy (Hayward Leach). Weddings, although they’re very joyous, sometimes bring families together in a way that can create some stress. It’s going to be fun to see what happens when Elsbeth’s mother comes, and we see a little bit more about the kind of upbringing that Elsbeth had, and the kind of mother that she was raised by, and parents. To learn about (why) Elsbeth wasn’t like the other kids growing up, and what that was like. Trying to fit in and all those things, which I think is going to just add more dimension and color to the character.

The thing that I love about our show is it’s not centered on a woman needing a man or feeling like a man completes her or she needs a man to make herself secure. Her primary relationship is with her work, and it’s with her son and her friends and reinventing herself at this age and stage in her life. That said, she’s someone who people are attracted to, and she is attracted to other people.

In the first episode, it was fun to play with the fact that sometimes you are attracted in a weird way to people that you are in opposition with. There’s sometimes a fine line between people who butt heads and people who kiss. Not that there’s anything going to happen with Smullen. I don’t know. I’m not in charge of the writing. But I do feel like it was a fun juxtaposition to what was happening with Nicole Scherzinger’s character in the episode. That’s just great writing, and I definitely trust our writers to take the character to places that I couldn’t even dream of.

There’s been a couple of times throughout the series where you see Elsbeth and Smullen connect in a way that is more personal. There are gentle little things where she’ll call him “Bobby.” When Bobby was so worried in the episode about the wigs that he wasn’t attractive, and so he got a wig himself, she said, “Bobby, you look great the way you are.” Just tender little things like that. I don’t think it’s a conscious thing on either of their parts. Just because you might have a kind or passing thought about someone doesn’t mean you’re going to act on it. But the will-they-won’t-they thing is what we were playing with in that first episode. I think the audience has definitely picked up on both of those things.

To the credit of our brilliant director of that episode, Nancy Hower — she’s the one who came to Danny Mastrogiorgio and I, and said, “Hey, why don’t we just go a little further for that moment? Let’s make it feel like, ‘Will they?’ at this moment.”

It turned into this tiny little thought, a little spark, a little something, which sometimes that’s the most delicious thing. The thing that you don’t act on. A little side note: Danny Mastrogiorgio and I went to Juilliard together, so we were classmates. I’ve known him for a very long time, so it was an interesting thing for us to play, and we certainly had a good time with it.

The writing, it’s all pretty centric around the wedding and the planning of the wedding, and what that does to Elsbeth when her mom’s around, when you’re self conscious about how you are in the world when you see yourself through your parents’ eyes. It’s hard sometimes not to feel like you’re somehow falling short. It’s enough to make Elsbeth a little vulnerable, having her mom in her workspace and in her home life and in the relationship between her and Teddy.

Kaya is continuing to be undercover, which is an exciting thing for that character because she really got to blossom from being a police officer to a detective, and now to (being) undercover. There will be a case that the NYPD is investigating that it turns out she’s undercover for, so then Elizabeth and Kaya get to have a little reunion.
I love working with Carra (Patterson).

There could potentially be a natural crossover because let’s not forget that Elsbeth is a lawyer. That’s a legal show. I would guess it would need to be that somehow one of these big tech guys that they’re investigating in “Cupertino” would be in New York, and they would have to come there. Maybe there’s some kind of police thing that happened, and the NYPD gets involved, and then we would have a nice little police-legal crossover. But I would never presume to even pitch a thing to Robert and Michelle King. They’re doing just fine without me.

Let’s see … I mean, it would be fun for Elsbeth to cross paths with Alicia Florrick (Julianna Margulies) again. The original appearance of Elsbeth was a more eccentric one. So it would be fun if she even just had coffee with Alicia.

I always say Meryl Streep. I’ll add Allison Janney to that. I couldn’t have even dreamt of some of, if not all of, the guest stars that we’ve had. So I also leave it in the capable hands of Findley Davidson and our exec producers to bring people to us. The teenage Carrie is always jumping up and down whenever I hear who’s going to be our next guest. A lot of them are people that I admired my whole career, and then I’m standing right in front of them and doing a scene with them, and it’s pretty extraordinary.

I really liked the finale of season three with Patti LuPone. We were in the fictitious version of the Cafe Carlyle. It was all very interesting and glamorous. And having Patti LuPone sing a song to me across the table, those kinds of moments are never to be forgotten.
I’ve been reading about this Kelly Clarkson thing that’s going on right now. (laughs) Maybe there’s something there.

title: She Saw Who She Was Marrying on ‘Love Is Blind,’ and Left. Jax Explains Her Sudden Decision
summary: Jax and Stewart speaks to TODAY.com about her ghosting him after their first in-person meeting in Season 11 of “Love Is Blind.”
story: Warning: Spoilers from “Love Is Blind” Season 11 below…
Jacqueline “Jax” Guelli and Scott “Stew” Stewart might hold the record for the shortest engagement in “Love Is Blind” history.

The two Bostonians met in Season 11 of the dating series, which arrived on Netflix Oct. 14. Jax and Stew hit it off in the pods, bonding over their refined tastes and their dreams for a luxurious wedding.

As the experiment continued, they opened up about their insecurities and pasts, with Stew sharing he had never been in love before. The reveal made Jax question if Stew was the right person for her, but she decided her feelings were too strong to walk away. He proposed and she accepted before their first in-person meeting.

When the two saw each other in Episode 4, they embraced as Jax repeated how “weird” the situation was. They shared a kiss but in her confessional interview immediately after, Jax told the cameras Stew more closely resembled Mitt Romney than a Kennedy, the nickname he said the male cast members had given him.
“I don’t want to be mean,” she whispered as a producer asked her to explain how she felt.

At the start of Episode 5, Stew was elated in his interview and complimented Jax’s appearance. But his feelings were not reciprocated as she told the producers she wanted to leave the show immediately. She also declined to meet with Stew.
Producers informed Stew of Jax’s departure and shared that she requested the show not give him her contact information.
Looking back at the experience, Jax tells TODAY.com that she felt “overwhelmed” after seeing Stew in person.
“This was all really new to me, so walking in there, it was just incredibly overwhelming. I felt like I was in a surreal dream, so I wasn’t really thinking,” she explains.

The 31-year-old entrepreneur continues, “But the connection wasn’t there, like for me at that moment. And there was just too much going on in my head. And I unfortunately didn’t deal with it well, how I wanted (to) or how I may have in real life. I just really wanted to get home.”
In a separate interview, Stew also shares how he processed the reveal and how it felt to learn Jax had quit the show.

“I think there’s so much going on at that reveal,” he recalls. “There’s so much pressure. It’s such a new experience. It’s something that nobody can prepare for. I don’t think I noticed what was maybe being sent out, and so it did come as a shock to me.”
But he didn’t appear to hold Jax’s response against her.

“I also think on the flip side, Jax deserves some degree of credit, some grace,” he adds. “She probably would have approached that differently had she had a different chance, had the emotions going through her mind not been going through her mind.”
Still, he says learning that his experiment had abruptly ended caught him off guard.

“But thinking back on the way that I carried myself and conducted myself in the pods, there was nothing that I really regretted there, and so the outcome was what it was. There were no ‘what ifs’ in my mind,” he tells TODAY.com.
When asked what he will take away from this experiment, Stew says he discovered a lot about himself after watching his conversations in the pods.

“I think what I learned is there’s a time for humor, there’s a time for jokes and there’s a time to be a little bit more serious, more sincere,” the 34-year-old director of engineering says. “Had I had the opportunity to do it again, maybe I would have shown that side a little more.”
As for Jax, she says she also learned a valuable lesson: “To not ghost people in real life.”
“And to own your own faults,” she adds.

Their time on the show isn’t over. A teaser at the end of Episode 5 showed the two reuniting to discuss their engagement. Fans will see how the conversation goes when episodes six through eight hit Netflix on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

title: Carson Greeted In Ireland By Group of Dalys After Learning Details of His Family History From the 1800s
summary: TODAY’s trip to Ireland has doubled as a homecoming for Carson Daly.
story: TODAY’s trip to Ireland has doubled as a homecoming for Carson Daly.

The TODAY co-host not only learned more about his family’s roots on the Emerald Isle, he was also surprised with heartwarming hugs from a group of Dalys in Kenmare in County Kerry, including his actual distant cousin.
It turns out that hundreds of years before Carson and his late mother became known for their work on television, the Daly family were coal miners in Ireland.
“This is every person’s dream is to figure out a little bit about where they come from,” Carson said on TODAY Oct. 16.
The TODAY co-host is one of more than 32 million Americans who claim Irish ancestry, a number six times greater than the entire population of the Emerald Isle.

To gain more insight into his family’s history, Carson enlisted the help of genealogist Fiona Fitzimons. She is the director of the Irish Family History Center at EPIC The Irish Emigration Museum in Dublin.
Unlike genealogy sites like Ancestry.com or the personal genetics company 23andMe, which use DNA to trace family origins, Fitzsimons and her team rely on birth, marriage and immigration records.
Carson’s sister, Quinn Daly, has served as his family’s historian over the years, and she was just as eager as Carson to find out more about their roots.
“We took the Ancestry test, but we don’t actually know the history,” Quinn said on TODAY. “Like we know the DNA part of it, but we don’t know the context.”
Their father, Jim Daly, died of bladder cancer in 1979 when Carson was 5 years old.
“We lost our dad at a very young age, and I think our family tree has been kind of a difficult one for us to track down,” Carson said.
Carson was able to see historical documents listing moments in his family’s history, thanks to Fitzsimons.
“We’ve got your family back to the early 1800s,” she said. “We found that your Dalys are colliers. They’re coal miners.”
That skill was particularly crucial for the family at the time.
“In the 1840s, we had a great famine, but your ancestors, because they were colliers, because they were skilled laborers, they actually had opportunities,” Fitzsimons told Carson.

“That is just blowing my mind,” Carson said. “You’re basically saying that my family was able to survive obviously one of the most devastating things that’s ever happened to the country because they had a skillset of a trade. I tell my kids who are going to college all the time. I’m always reminding them of the trades.”
Carson also learned that the woman his great-grandfather married in 1903 was named Mary Quinn, whose last name is now Carson’s sister’s first name.
“I don’t even know if we knew it was a family name,” Carson said.
Fitzsimons mapped out Carson’s lineage to three regions in Ireland — Ballinagleragh and Kiltoghert in County Leitrim, and Crettyard in County Laois.
She pinpointed that his ancestors on his mother and father’s sides both immigrated to America and met in New Jersey.

“This makes me an absolute badass by bloodline,” Carson said. “The families come together and survive and thrive and fight wars in India, and then all end up drinking Guinness in New Jersey, and ultimately this kid’s born in California.”
Carson also learned that he may have relatives who remained in Ireland. Daly is one of the 15 most common last names in the country.

“We found that there are some Dalys still in the same parish and even in the same townland that your family came from,” Fitzsimons said. “Certainly, up until the last five years, so it’s possible that you have family members that remain behind, that survived and continued.”
Carson wondered if one of those relatives might be Paul Hewson.
“Is there any chance I’m related to Bono?” he asked.
“Statistically, it’s totally possible, but, ummm...” Fitzsimons said while laughing.

Savannah Guthrie surprised Carson on the streets of Kenmare with a meet-up among a group of Dalys. After sharing hugs, he was presented with a framed flag of Ireland by a local senator and met face to face with a distant cousin from his paternal grandfather’s side named Lorraine.
“There’s no place like home,” Lorraine told Carson in Gaelic. “And the other thing I wanted to say is, ‘You may leave Ireland, but Ireland will always be with you.’”
